checks.s: Section 2.01 sets the proposed compromise permanent easement width at 140 feet.
The proposed compromise temporary construction easement is 65 feet per side.
The deliverable states that the 140-ft permanent easement corridor is approximately 19.02 acres.
The easement-width fallback ladder gives Grantor at least three concession rungs from its 80 ft opening position toward the compromise zone.
The easement-width fallback ladder gives Grantee at least three concession rungs from its 200 ft opening position toward the compromise zone.
The compensation-structure fallback ladder gives Grantor at least three concession rungs from its opening position toward the compromise zone.
The compensation-structure fallback ladder gives Grantee at least three concession rungs from its opening position toward the compromise zone.
The restoration/vegetation management/fencing fallback ladder gives Grantor at least three concession rungs from its opening position toward the compromise zone.
The restoration/vegetation management/fencing fallback ladder gives Grantee at least three concession rungs from its opening position toward the compromise zone.
The termination/abandonment/assignment fallback ladder gives Grantor at least three concession rungs from its opening position toward the compromise zone.
The termination/abandonment/assignment fallback ladder gives Grantee at least three concession rungs from its opening position toward the compromise zone.
The proposed compromise signing payment is between $195,000 and $215,000, approximately $205,000.
The deliverable states or demonstrates that the approximately $205,000 signing payment exceeds the Elliston midpoint diminution of $155,000.
The proposed compromise annual payment is between $8,000 and $9,500, approximately $8,750.
The annual payment escalator is tied to CPI-U (West Region), rather than a fixed percentage.
The CPI-U escalator has a floor of 1.0 or equivalent language that prevents a year-over-year decrease in the annual payment.
The clause provides for a 3% fixed escalation rate if the CPI-U index is discontinued.
The crop/forage-loss payment uses a 125% multiplier.
The crop-loss payment is based on USDA county yield data.

The compromise defines an Organic Buffer Zone adjacent to the USDA-certified organic parcels that is approximately 100–200 feet wide and permits only mechanical vegetation management, with no synthetic herbicides.
The compromise includes an indemnification clause protecting Grantor against loss of organic certification caused by Grantee's activities and references Cert. No. NV-ORG-2021-00547.
The compromise requires permanent four-strand barbed-wire cattle fencing on both sides of the corridor.
The compromise requires Grantee to pay the fencing cost in full.
Grantee is responsible for fencing maintenance for an initial period of approximately 5 years.
After the initial period, fencing maintenance responsibility transfers to Grantor, except for damage caused by Grantee's activities.
The abandonment trigger is 30–36 consecutive months of non-operation, approximately 33 months.
The abandonment clause tolls the non-use period for force majeure events.
The abandonment clause reasonably addresses additional documented tolling categories, including government-ordered or regulatory outages and active reconstruction or capital improvement.
After the abandonment trigger period elapses, the abandonment provision gives Grantee 150–210 days, approximately 180 days, to resume operations or submit a resumption plan.
The removal obligation specifies a defined removal period of 12–18 months, approximately 15 months.
The removal obligation covers all above-ground and near-surface structures.
The removal obligation places the removal cost solely on Grantee.
The compromise requires a removal security instrument in the approximate range of $112,500–$140,000.
The removal security instrument has a credit-quality floor requirement.
Third-party assignments require Grantor's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.
The assignment provision exempts affiliate transfers from the consent requirement.
The assignment provision exempts successor-entity transfers through merger, consolidation, or sale of substantially all project assets from the consent requirement.
The assignment provision requires any assignee to provide a written assumption agreement.
The transfer fee for non-exempt third-party assignments is between $8,000 and $12,500, approximately $10,000.
The compromise uses a jointly approved seed mix rather than a mix specified unilaterally by Grantor or set as Grantee's standard mix.
The seed-mix cost cap is between $350 and $425 per acre, near $400 per acre.
The compromise provides for a neutral third-party tiebreaker, such as a licensed rangeland-management consultant, if the parties cannot agree on the seed mix.
Grantee bears all seeding and reseeding costs.
The temporary construction easement automatically expires 16–20 months after commencement, approximately 18 months.
The temporary construction easement may be extended by mutual written agreement for up to 6 months.
The compromise preserves Grantor's grazing, farming, and irrigation uses within the easement corridor, subject to reasonable restrictions protecting transmission operations.

Each proposed compromise clause across the four contested term categories is accompanied by a written rationale explaining why its language is defensible to both Grantor and Grantee and addressing relevant engineering, agricultural, financial, or legal justifications.
The compromise package favors Grantor on organic-certification protection.
The compromise package favors Grantor on fencing.
The compromise package favors Grantee on assignment flexibility through affiliate and lender carve-outs.
The abandonment trigger is at least 36 months, favoring Grantee's lender requirement.
The rationale acknowledges Grantor's flexibility on corridor width if compensation is satisfactory and explains how the compromise reflects that trade-off.
The deliverable calculates the per-acre signing payment using the approximately 19.02-acre compromise corridor and references the appraised land value of $5,500 per acre.
The deliverable demonstrates that the signing payment is a defensible multiple of $5,500 per acre, such as approximately $205,000 ÷ 19.02 acres ≈ $10,778 per acre ≈ 1.96×.
The compromise references the NV PUC CPCN construction-start deadline of March 3, 2026 as a factor in the negotiation dynamics or timeline provisions.

The deliverable references the 14 comparable permanent transmission-line easement transactions in NV, OR, ID, and UT from 2020–2025 to support the proposed compromise terms and show that the positions fall within market ranges.

The compromise places enforceable drift-prevention controls on herbicide application outside the Organic Buffer Zone, such as a dormant-season spray window approximately October 1 through March 31, advance written notice to Grantor, or wind-speed or application-method limits.
For herbicide use outside the Organic Buffer Zone, the compromise limits products to a defined or approved set and provides Grantor visibility or periodic review of permitted products.

The deliverable includes an overall compromise package summary table identifying which party's position each contested sub-term is closer to and showing rough balance, with each party winning approximately half of the sub-terms closer to its opening position.
The deliverable is presented as ready for the August 11, 2025 principals' meeting.
The assignment clause states that the original Grantee is not relieved of its obligations absent a written release from Grantor.
The assignment provision states that any purported assignment in violation of the provision is void.

The compromise language identifies and corrects the standard-form easement agreement's Grantee-favorable conventions, including broad operational flexibility and minimal Grantor consent requirements, to achieve balanced provisions.

The rationale calculates and discloses the effective worst-case total non-use period before reversion as 36–42 months, combining the 30–36-month abandonment trigger with the 6-month notice-and-cure period.
The rationale explains why the 36–42-month total is workable for both sides, giving Grantee a buffer at or above the 36-month lender minimum and giving Grantor a defined, enforceable process.
